This game feels amazing to play. Once you get past the first few levels and start grasping the controls, you start to enter a trance-like state that is very rewarding. The immediate death resets, fast pace, and carefully progressive challenge create an addictive loop of rewarding game play. It feels a lot like Hotline Miami, where you can do the same thing 100 times, slowly inching towards your goal each time, until you finally achieve it and get a huge rush of euphoria.

The only problem this game has is the abrupt difficulty jump in the penultimate world, Mercury. it feels as thought 2 or 3 worlds were missing before it to build up player skill and game feel, and you're left floundering. For a game that is completely lucid during the previous 7 worlds, it can really leave a sour taste in a player's mouth at the end. combine that with the fact every level must be beaten in order to finish the game, and i'd imagine most people give up/switch to easy mode to complete the campaign. 

Even with such a strong difficulty spike, this game is a blast to play and will consume you for a couple hours at the very least. Highly recommended.

Flywrench, overall, is a very fun and pleasant game.
Up until Mercury.
I love the art choices, adore the music, and generally appreciate the loose story surrounding it. The game really deserves more love.
However. Reaching Mercury after returning to the game and playing through each planet in under an hour total, I was mortified to find how wretched it was in every regard.
Mercury highlights many major flaws in the game's engine and physics system, and each level would take over an hour to properly finish until I had gotten through each one.
Up to this point, each death had felt fair, deserved, and entirely my fault.
After Mercury, I had myself genuinely questioning if this game was intended to be RAGE BAIT.
A number of levels on the planet effectively boiled down to luck on your timing, praying the physics wouldn't jank out and send you flying into a wall at mach 3, or just Being Lucky with your frames. It was just pure garbage level design on some levels, effectively just repeatedly dying to a randomly placed obstacle that was likely only put in to artificially elevate the difficulty of the final proper gate.
Despite my pure loathing for this section of the game, I still overall give it glowing regards and strongly suggest it to anyone willing to set aside a couple hours. It was very entertaining and borderline enthralling at some sections. I almost hope a sequel is made, though given it's been over a decade, I strongly doubt it will ever happen.

The entire story can be beaten within a couple hours, especially when the game's unique aesthetics and mesmerizing yet energizing music puts you into a "flow state". If you're a fan of platforming games, the experience is well worth the price.

Flywrench is an assault on the senses, but I loved it for that. Glitchy, noisy, constant graphical motion. In the character, the levels, the menu transitions. Almost nothing is static here. The soundtrack is a perfect fit, and really brings the whole thing together.

Gameplay is essentially flappy bird mini golf, but on a controller drifting around feels great.

If you just do the story mode, it's probably 2-3 hours depending on how good you are. I'm okay I think. Time trials and workshop support extend that further if you really fall in love.

As a way to unwind for 20-30 minutes over the course of a week, Flywrench is an easy recommendation I think. On sale, even easier. And if you're on the fence after reading about it or watching a trailer, the demo is more than enough to give you an idea of whether or not you can spare the time and money.
